armenelos-world

  • The vault holds all 543 restore points in 2.18 GB: 0.14% of the 1.58 TB of uncompressed working trees, 19.70% of the 11.09 GB git repository, and 1.25x one full snapshot.
  • The baseline wrote 332.93 MB (15.2% of the vault); the other 542 restore points added 1.85 GB in total.
  • Median append after the baseline is 92.81 kB (0.01% of a full snapshot). The largest is snapshot 9 (00009-20200907-193349-dfe0f11) at 527.82 MB, with 209,723 new and 118,103 changed targets.
  • All FULL and DELTA blocks round-tripped byte-for-byte.

Storage over time

Everything is expressed in units of one full snapshot of the last version. Blue: the engine's append-only vault. Purple: the git repository holding the same commits. Green: one full snapshot.

What each snapshot costs

Bars use a log scale because the baseline is two orders of magnitude larger than steady state. The dashed line is the same append as a percentage of a full snapshot.

Where the append goes

Stacked bytes per append: new targets must be written in full; changed targets pay only a delta; headers and the block index cache are fixed overhead. The baseline is omitted because it is entirely new-target FULL payload.

Target churn

Changed, new and deleted targets per snapshot. The baseline has no diff by definition.

File activity over time

Each column is one region/entity/poi file or tracked .dat; the 18 most active files are shown. Colour = changed + new targets in that snapshot. Vertical stripes show where the world actually moved. Rows are sampled: 170 of 543 commits.

Target families

Chunk versus whole-file appends per snapshot, log scale, baseline omitted. A family that is persistently high is where tuning pays off.

Codec comparison

Only one configuration in this study. Re-run with --levels 3,9 --long off,on to compare codecs.

Targets aggregated across every snapshot, ranked by total DELTA bytes. Small DELTA/FULL ratios mean alignment and the delta coder are doing their job.

Raw data

Every number in this report comes from these files. They are plain CSV and can be opened in any spreadsheet; changes.csv lists each new, changed and deleted target.

  • zstd L3 / default: versions.csv · families.csv · regions.csv · changes.csv.xz · skipped.csv

Method, accounting and caveats

Model. Every snapshot is a complete world copy. Each is scanned into the targets the engine tracks: every non-empty chunk in region/, entities/ and poi/ .mca files (including custom dimensions), plus level.dat, playerdata/*.dat and every data/ .dat. All 543 versions are compared with the previous one by canonical NBT bytes, and the checkpoint policy is replayed: the first version writes a FULL baseline; a changed target appends a DELTA against its previous visible block; a new target appends FULL + an ABSENT marker; a deleted target appends an ABSENT marker; an unchanged target appends nothing. Every block is decompressed and byte-compared (roundtrip_fail).

Accounting. The 42-byte block header, the per-block index cache entry and the 28-byte per-file cache header are included. Filesystem block rounding and index.properties are not. "Full snapshot" is the cost of writing every current target as FULL with the same cache, i.e. what one independent full backup would cost.

Caveats. Diff is content-based, not write-capture: a target is "changed" only when its canonical bytes differ, so a server that rewrites identical data would append a small delta in production that is not charged here (the incremental numbers are a lower bound). Files outside the tracked NBT scope (datapacks, JSON, configs) are counted in "World" but not stored in the vault. Append-only, no GC or keyframes. Timings are a single warm-cache run on this machine, so treat them as indicative; byte counts are deterministic.

Engine. $MINIMAL_BACKUP at ef7566fdc1e2a3d3..., 32 source files.

Git input. https://github.com/armenelos/world at master: 4,574 commits, 543 effective and 4,031 skipped. A commit is effective when it changes at least one file the engine tracks; commits that only touch README files, logs, session.lock or level.dat_old are skipped. Each effective commit is materialised into one live directory by tools/git_materialize.py immediately before it is scanned, and the preparation time is reported separately (prepare_ms). Source bytes are the sum of working-tree file sizes at that commit, i.e. an uncompressed checkout; the git repository size is the packed size reported by git count-objects. World roots: ..

Reproduce. bench.py run --manifest $BENCH_BASE/datasets/armenelos-world/manifest.tsv --raw-manifest --meta $BENCH_BASE/datasets/armenelos-world/dataset.json --name armenelos-world --levels 3 --heap 18g --force
